title: "Estimation"
format: html
---

## Initial nonlinear fit

PGM first fits the selected Unified growth equation using nonlinear least squares and the Levenberg--Marquardt algorithm [@nlsLM].

The initial fit serves two purposes:

1. it provides the final estimates for an ordinary nonlinear model;
2. it provides starting values for GNLS or NLME estimation when additional model structures are requested.

## Final estimation framework

An ordinary NLS fit is retained when the model contains only the growth equation.

GNLS is used when no random effects are specified but the model contains one or more of:

- fixed-effect predictors;
- a residual variance function;
- an AR(1) or CAR(1) residual correlation structure.

NLME is used whenever at least one growth parameter contains a random effect.

NLME models are estimated by maximum likelihood using the `nlme` framework [@nlme].

## Parameter-specific fixed effects

Each estimated growth parameter has its own fixed-effects formula.

For example,

$$
\log(A)
=
\beta_{A0}
+
\beta_{A1}X
$$

and

$$
\log(K)
=
\beta_{K0}
+
\beta_{K1}Z
+
\beta_{K2}Q
+
\beta_{K3}ZQ
$$

may be fitted simultaneously.

A parameter with no assigned predictors is represented by an intercept-only formula.

## Parameter transformations

Positive parameters are fitted on transformed scales.

The principal internal transformations are:

$$
A=\exp(\alpha),
$$

$$
K=\exp(\kappa),
$$

$$
d=\exp(\lambda)
$$

for free Richards shape, and

$$
\eta_0=
\operatorname{logit}\left(\frac{W_0}{A}\right)
$$

under the `W0` parameterization.

$T_i$ is fitted directly on its natural time scale.

When the asymptote is fixed, $A$ is removed from the estimated parameter vector.

## Fixed-effect design validation

Before GNLS or NLME estimation, PGM removes unused factor levels and checks the requested fixed-effects structure.

Categorical predictors must retain at least two observed levels.

The model matrix for each growth parameter must also have full column rank.

Empty factor combinations, redundant interactions, or perfectly collinear predictors therefore produce an informative error rather than an unidentified fit.

## Natural-scale parameter profiles

The model is fitted on its estimation scale, but the parameter table reports values on the natural growth-parameter scale.

For categorical predictors, the first observed factor level is used as the reference level.

For continuous predictors, the reference profile is evaluated at zero.

Rows corresponding to continuous effects represent the parameter profile at a predictor value of one relative to the zero reference profile.

For interactions, the reported natural-scale parameter value includes the associated main-effect and interaction contributions required by that predictor profile.

## Standard errors

The covariance matrix is obtained on the model estimation scale.

For a reported natural-scale quantity

$$
g(\boldsymbol\theta),
$$

PGM uses a first-order delta approximation:

$$
\operatorname{Var}
\left[
g(\hat{\boldsymbol\theta})
\right]
\approx
J
\operatorname{Var}
(\hat{\boldsymbol\theta})
J^\mathsf{T},
$$

where $J$ is the Jacobian of the transformation evaluated at the corresponding parameter profile.

For $W_0$, uncertainty propagation includes its joint dependence on both the asymptote and the internal initial-value parameter when $A$ is estimated.

## Confidence intervals

Approximate 95% confidence intervals are derived from the fitted covariance matrix and the corresponding transformed parameter profile.

For positive transformed parameters, interval limits are returned to the natural parameter scale.

For $W_0$, PGM uses a log-scale delta approximation for the positive natural-scale quantity.

These intervals are asymptotic approximations and may be unreliable when:

- sample size or effective replication is small;
- parameters are weakly identified;
- the observed trajectory poorly covers the relevant part of the curve;
- the fixed-effects design is nearly singular;
- the fitted model is numerically unstable.

## Fixed-effect p-values

When fixed effects are present, PGM reports coefficient-level p-values obtained from the fitted NLS/GNLS/NLME model on the model estimation scale.

These are tests of individual model coefficients.

They are not automatically omnibus tests of an entire multi-level factor or interaction term.

For categorical predictors, coefficients are interpreted relative to the reference level.

For interactions, the reported p-value corresponds to the relevant interaction coefficient on the estimation scale.
